helper_dispatch.conclusion: Exported execvp is not an unconditional helper boundary. Actual mode/env/file values are required to determine which import is used. Imported execvp and a public-source call alone cannot establish that the native attempt invoked it.

Frida_lifecycle.actual_Java_sequence: Held exec event -> Session.start (attach_sync) -> enableChildGating_sync -> create QJS options(runtime1), create script, connect message receiver, load_sync -> manager.resume. The scratch driver polls installed messages only in the later outer loop, so it did not explicitly verify a ready message or executable identity between load and resume.
Frida_lifecycle.automatic_flush: Pinned QuickJS gumjs_send ends and begins the interceptor transaction BEFORE message_emitter. The tested script calls send(installed) after all Interceptor.attach operations. This already performs the same transaction boundary as explicit Interceptor.flush; adding flush alone is not a source-supported explanation of the observed gap.
Frida_lifecycle.child_gating_guards: Agent.enable_child_gating starts and ends a Gum interceptor transaction while installing ForkMonitor, FileDescriptorGuard, FD/thread cloakers and SpawnMonitor. On ordinary Linux SpawnMonitor attaches exported libc execve, not execvp.
Frida_lifecycle.descriptor_closure_counterevidence: The actual helper closes descriptors greater than5 and directly closes4/5 before JDK_execvpe. This is not proof that it kills Frida IPC: pinned FileDescriptorGuard intercepts close from outside the agent and substitutes fd=-1/success for cloaked descriptors, while FDListCloaker hides those descriptors from procfs listings. Guard installation/liveness in this native transition was not independently observed.
Frida_lifecycle.what_installed_proves: The JS top-level ran in a process with the reported PID, architecture, libc path and resolved export addresses and emitted the ready payload. Source-supported patch transaction synchronization precedes that emission.
what_it_does_not_prove: Which executable was Process.mainModule at ready time; only PID/libc were logged.
The original application-thread PC or whether it had already passed the helper local entry during attachment.
Actual bytes/GOT resolution of the hook target after commit.
The image/session lifetime through the subsequent exec; no script-destroyed or session-detached timeline was retained.
That a successful script install makes the required action callback run.

wrapper_and_action_topology.observed_wait_boundary: JVM3011 returned children3207,3288,3296,3314,3321. None equals action stdout PIDs3295,3308,3322,3333. The four latter action PPids match the four successful JVM-reaped PIDs; this is compatible with a wrapper hop, not an action-status receipt.
wrapper_and_action_topology.actual_Bazel_class_bytecode: LocalSpawnRunner$SubprocessHandler in the identical A-server.jar conditionally builds a ProcessWrapper-prefixed command, starts SubprocessBuilder and calls waitFor/exitValue. Actual JavaSubprocessFactory invokes ProcessBuilder.start; its JavaSubprocess calls Process.waitFor. The native receipt does not independently capture whether the wrapper branch was taken.

actual_wrapper_machine_code.SpawnChild: 0x4078b7 fork; returned child PID stored at0x4078bc; child branch setsid/clears signals/umask and calls execvp at0x4078f9
actual_wrapper_machine_code.WaitForChild: 0x407a58 calls WaitChildWithRusage when statistics path is nonempty; alternate0x407ac2 calls WaitChild
actual_wrapper_machine_code.subreaper: SpawnChild attempts prctl at0x4078a7 and sets child_subreaper_enabled on success; unsupported EINVAL may leave it false. Success was not recorded dynamically.
actual_wrapper_machine_code.wait_APIs: WaitChildWithRusage at0x408c40 calls wait3 at0x408ca7 when subreaper is enabled; otherwise wait4 at0x408c74. WaitChild similarly chooses wait versus waitpid. The prior scratch probe hooked only waitpid/wait4.
actual_wrapper_machine_code.normal_exit_mapping: WaitForChild tests low7 signal bits and on normal exit uses the high status byte at0x407b57 then exit. Signal/time-limit and cleanup paths can differ. This code mapping is not a substitute for capturing a given action raw wait status.

wrapper_and_action_topology.genuine_action_result_requirement: After independently identifying the actual wrapper image, observe its original wait/wait3/waitpid/wait4 returned PID and status pointer for the authenticated action PID; preserve the parent reaping and original return unchanged. Capturing only JVM waits cannot establish this. No fail23, replay or action-status equivalence has been inferred.

smallest_next_probe_contract.inputs: Reuse exact accepted Frida SO/JDK/Bazel producer hashes and unchanged tiny fixture. sequence: At held helper event independently capture procfs exe symlink/hash and existing kernel PPid/cgroup identity before attachment.

In the loaded script record Process.mainModule identity/base and main-thread context where available; resolve actual ELF-local childProcess and JDK_execvpe symbols through Module APIs, and capture execvp/execve import addresses/slots alongside the libc export addresses.

Install minimal local JDK_execvpe, optional childProcess marker, and exported execvp/execve observers. Retain original target bytes before attachment and committed bytes after the send/flush transaction. Do not parse ChildStuff fields or mutate GOT/argv/env/cwd/descriptors/results.

Emit ready after instrumentation; Java must actually receive and validate ready and re-read procfs exe identity before Manager.resume. No top-level recv.wait that deadlocks synchronous script loading.

At JDK_execvpe entry copy mode/file/argv/envp directly from four ABI arguments; hold only inside this real callback until the Java owner acknowledges. This is launch context for the next image, potentially a wrapper, not yet the final action boundary.
Compare actual helper local entry/mode, import resolution, committed target bytes and image identities. Retain missing/lost observations as unknown and stop rather than synthesizing a classification.

Only after the helper-to-next-image hop is understood, use existing child gating to identify and instrument the real wrapper image and its forked action. Add read-only wait/wait3 as well as waitpid/wait4 observation in the actual parent; no replacement parent or custom SpawnRunner.

discriminators.conditional_export_miss: A local JDK entry with observed mode/env/file selects the actual binary dispatch; mode3 with distinct env and slash file expects execve, not execvp.
discriminators.import_target_miss: Actual module import/GOT target differs from the recorded hooked export address after resolution; retain exact address/module/version evidence rather than assume all exec symbols are equivalent.
discriminators.uncommitted_patch: Compare captured target bytes before and after the acknowledged send/flush boundary. Source already flushes on send, so missing manual flush alone is contradicted; an actual missing/incorrect patch needs native evidence.
discriminators.image_or_timing_change: Procfs executable hash and Process.mainModule disagree across event/attach/ready/resume, or main-thread context is already beyond a local entry. This requires exact observations, not a PID or installed message alone.
discriminators.still_inconclusive: Same helper image and committed target bytes without the expected local callback remains unknown; do not claim root cause or widen to custom Bazel.

smallest_next_probe_contract.acceptance: Actual required pre-execution callback with exact unmodified context and trusted image lineage; then original-parent direct action results including23. Source availability or script installation passes only availability. Replay authority remains a separate unproved boundary.
